from.place: Proof paragraph 2, the displayed derived coefficient mapping-complex adjunction: evaluation at an identity extracts the universal map from a representing equivalence before applying the local coherent adjoint criterion.

title: Infinity Yoneda evaluation at the identity
statement:
Fix universes $\mathcal U\in\mathcal U'$, and use quasicategories, mapping spaces and coherent transformations as in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Let $\mathcal E$ be a $\mathcal U'$-small quasicategory and have $\mathcal U$-small mapping spaces, let $\mathcal S$ denote the infinity category of $\mathcal U$-small spaces, and let $a\in\mathcal E$. Form the concrete rigidification functors of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces] for $\mathcal E$ and $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ first in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$, the infinity category of $\mathcal U\prime$-small spaces. Each admits a coherent $\mathcal S$-valued model: this means a functor into $\mathcal S$ equipped with a coherent natural equivalence, after the inclusion $\mathcal S\hookrightarrow\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$, to the corresponding concrete functor. Choose any such models; their distinguished identity points correspond under these equivalences to the singular identity vertices, up to the specified homotopies. Write $h_a(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)$ for the resulting coherent representable presheaf; mapping-space notation here denotes its value up to the comparison equivalence, rather than equality of underlying simplicial sets. For every coherent presheaf $P:\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}\to\mathcal S$, evaluation at $\operatorname{id}_a$ induces an equivalence of spaces
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(h_a,P)\simeq P(a),\qquad \alpha\longmapsto\alpha_a(\operatorname{id}_a).$$
Its inverse sends $p\in P(a)$ to the coherent transformation whose component at $x$ is $f\mapsto P(f)(p)$ for $f:x\to a$. Thus for any coherent transformation $\alpha:h_a\to P$, its component maps are homotopic to $f\mapsto P(f)(\alpha_a(\operatorname{id}_a))$, coherently in $x$ and in parameters in the mapping spaces. Dually, for $Q:\mathcal E\to\mathcal S$ and $h^a(x)=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a,x)$, evaluation gives $\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E,\mathcal S)}(h^a,Q)\simeq Q(a)$ with inverse $q\mapsto(f\mapsto Q(f)(q))$. These are equivalences of full spaces of coherent transformations, not just bijections on homotopy classes.

source.place: Kerodon Proposition 8.3.1.3 (03M5), with evaluation defined in Notation 8.3.1.2 (03M4); apply also to the opposite category. Definition 5.6.6.1 (038A) gives the action on a universal element, and Theorem 5.6.6.13 (038J) supplies the coherent representable functor. Read online; not archived in literature/. These are Kerodon identifiers; no corresponding Stacks tag states this infinity-categorical assertion.

proof.text:
Work first covariantly in $C$, with $a\in C$, and take the actual rigidification functor $H$ of [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces]. Put $A=\mathfrak C[C]$, $M_x=\operatorname{Map}^{R}_C(a,x)$, and let $\eta\in H(a)$ be the singular identity vertex. Let $\lambda_x$ be the identity-action cocone and $e_x:M_x\to H(x)$ its point map, exactly as specified in [lem-coef-rigidification-identity-action]. That lemma identifies the actual map by the equation
$$[e_x][p_{M_x}]=[u_{a,x}][\theta_{C,a,x}].$$
Both $p_{M_x}$ and $\theta_{C,a,x}$ are weak homotopy equivalences by [lem-coef-pinched-rigidification-resolution]; $u_{a,x}$ is a weak homotopy equivalence for the arbitrary simplicial set $A(a,x)$ by [lem-cbc-realization-singular-unit-weak]. Hence $[e_x]$ is invertible. The weak-equivalence clause of [lem-coef-rigidification-identity-action] asserts this conclusion for the actual simplicial point map $e_x$. As spaces are considered up to weak homotopy equivalence, it is an equivalence of full spaces. This proves that $\eta$ is a universal identity element for the defined functor. It is a theorem proved here, not an additional hypothesis or a change of the definition. Take the value universe here to be $\mathcal U\prime$, so the concrete $H$ is defined: its rigidification is a colimit over a $\mathcal U\prime$-small simplex category and all its mapping simplicial sets and singular realizations are $\mathcal U\prime$-small. Local smallness does not imply that these concrete values are $\mathcal U$-small. Step 5 will construct coherent smaller models using the proved equivalences $e_x$ and $\mathcal U$-small Kan complexes weakly equivalent to $M_x$.

source.place: Section 2.2.4 opening paragraph and Proposition 2.2.4.1; Section 5.1.3 construction. Identity-action formula and two-out-of-three expanded explicitly.

proof.text: For $x\in C$, [lem-coef-infinity-slice-right-fibration] identifies the strict fiber $\{a\}\times_C C_{/x}$ with $M_x$. Its universal-arrow family is the right-pinch prism of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. Thus the local cocone induced by the point $\eta:*\to H(a)$ is exactly $\lambda_x$ of [lem-coef-rigidification-identity-action], not an arbitrarily chosen cocone with apex $H(x)$. Step 1 proves that its point map $e_x$ is a weak equivalence. By [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion], this actual cocone is colimiting. Apply that criterion with $\mathcal W=\mathcal U\prime$. Here $M_x\subseteq C_{n+1}$ degreewise is $\mathcal U\prime$-small because $C$ is, while $H(x)$ is $\mathcal U\prime$-small by Step 1; no $\mathcal U$-smallness of $M_x$ is used in this step. No colimit indexed by the whole ambient category is used.

source.place: Lemma 8.3.1.7, proof: actual identity-action cocone on the mapping-space index; with Example 7.1.2.10.

proof.text:
Take $K=\Delta^0$, $\delta:K\to C$ the vertex $a$, $F_0=*$, $F=H$, and $\beta=\eta$ in [lem-coef-pointwise-lan-mapping-property]. Its local indexing object at $x$ is exactly $M_x$, and its local cocone is the one proved colimiting in Step 2. For every $Q:C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$, the conclusion gives an equivalence
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime})}(H,Q)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}}(*,Q(a)),\qquad\alpha\longmapsto\alpha_a\eta.$$
The case $K=\Delta^0$ of [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion] identifies the target with $Q(a)$ by its family-of-points map. The resulting equivalence is consequently the specified evaluation $\Phi(\alpha)=\alpha_a(\operatorname{id}_a)$. All functor categories are formed in a universe containing $\mathcal U'$, as permitted by the cited theorem; this establishes evaluation first for the concrete larger-valued functor, before the descent in Step 5.

source.place: Proposition 8.3.1.3, proof via Lemma 8.3.1.7 and Proposition 7.3.6.1; Notation 8.3.1.2 specifies evaluation.

proof.text:
Let $\Phi$ be the full-space evaluation equivalence from Step 3, and choose a homotopy inverse $s$ with both inverse homotopies. For a transformation $\alpha:H\to Q$, its naturality, evaluated on the right-pinch arrow family and the point $\eta$, gives a homotopy of maps on the whole space $M_x$:
$$\alpha_x\circ e_x\simeq\bigl(f\longmapsto Q(f)(\alpha_a(\eta))\bigr).$$
Here $e_x$ is the comparison of [lem-coef-rigidification-identity-action]. It is not being replaced by a right-pinched composition law on the different complex $H(x)$. To check the stated homotopy with parameters, first apply the natural right-pinch map of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] in $\operatorname{Fun}(C,\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime})$. This sends the full right-pinched transformation space to the fixed-endpoint arrow space; its internal evaluation supplies a map $C\times T\times\Delta^1\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$ for the whole parameter space $T$. Evaluate it on the prism $M_x\times\Delta^1\to C$, and evaluate its constant starting value on $\eta$. The square is the simplicial map $(m,s,t)\mapsto\alpha(j(m,s),t)$ from $M_x\times\Delta^1\times\Delta^1$ to $\mathcal S$, where $j$ is the pinch prism. Its boundaries at $t=0,1$ are respectively the $H$-action and $Q$-action, and at $s=0,1$ they are respectively the constant families $\alpha_a$ and $\alpha_x$. The two triangle faces of the square compare its two composite paths. Precomposing their common starting point with $\eta$ gives exactly the two maps in the displayed homotopy. For an arbitrary simplex of the transformation mapping space, do the same with that simplex as an additional factor. The evaluation and restriction maps of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] commute with faces and degeneracies, so these are restrictions of one parameterized naturality square. The point-family equivalence of [lem-coef-space-point-cocone-criterion] turns it into the displayed homotopy of Kan-space maps, compatibly with every parameter. Step 1 makes $e_x$ an equivalence and identifies its identity point. Substituting $\alpha=s(q)$ and using $\Phi s\simeq\operatorname{id}$ therefore says that the inverse transformation has component $f\mapsto Q(f)(q)$, where the mapping-space notation for the value of the representable is interpreted through the proved $e_x$. The other inverse homotopy $s\Phi\simeq\operatorname{id}$ proves reconstruction for every $\alpha$. This produces the inverse on the whole space $Q(a)$, rather than choosing transformations separately for its vertices, and proves the larger-valued covariant clause with all coherence parameters.

source.place: Definition 5.6.6.1 specifies action on an element; parameterized naturality gives the inverse formula once Step 3 proves evaluation is an equivalence.

proof.text: Descend to the stipulated smaller value universe without asserting that the concrete $H(x)$ has a small underlying set. Let $\iota:\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$ be inclusion. By the coherent-nerve definition in [def-coef-infinity-category-of-spaces], it is a full simplicial subset: every enriched simplex whose vertices are smaller Kan complexes has exactly the same enriched Hom data in either universe. Hence its right-pinched mapping spaces are literally identical, so it is fully faithful. For each $x$, the map $e_x:M_x\to H(x)$ of Step 1 is a weak equivalence between Kan complexes ($M_x$ is Kan by [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]). We first produce a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex $Y_x$ and a weak equivalence $g_x:Y_x\to H(x)$; the mapping-space hypothesis of the statement concerns $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}$, and is not assumed to make $M_x$ itself a $\mathcal U$-small simplicial set. Covariant case $C=\mathcal E$: the hypothesis gives a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex $Y_x$ and a weak equivalence between $Y_x$ and $M_x=\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(a,x)$ (take $Y_x=M_x$ when $M_x$ is literally $\mathcal U$-small); if it points from $M_x$ to $Y_x$, replace it by the simplicial inverse of [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse], which is again a weak equivalence. Call the resulting map $k_x:Y_x\to M_x$. Contravariant case $C=\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$: take a $\mathcal U$-small Kan complex $Y'$ with a weak equivalence $Y'\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)$ as just described, and put $Y_x=Y'^{\mathrm{op}}$. Order reversal carries $\Lambda^n_i$ to $\Lambda^n_{n-i}$, so opposites of Kan complexes are Kan; the barycentric reversal $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|T|$ written out in Step 6 shows that opposites of weak equivalences are weak equivalences, and opposites of simplicial homotopies are simplicial homotopies because $(\Delta^1)^{\mathrm{op}}\cong\Delta^1$. Interval reversal gives $U_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,x)=U_{\mathcal E}(x,a)^{\mathrm{op}}$ (Step 6). Compose $Y'^{\mathrm{op}}\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)^{\mathrm{op}}\xrightarrow{j^{\mathrm{op}}}U_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,x)$ with a homotopy inverse of the homotopy equivalence $j_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},a,x}:M_x\to U_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,x)$; both $j$ maps are those of [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison]. This gives a weak equivalence $k_x:Y_x\to M_x$. In both cases put $g_x=e_xk_x$, a weak equivalence of Kan complexes with $\mathcal U$-small source. By [lem-cbc-kan-whitehead-inverse] it has a simplicial inverse and two homotopies. Apply [lem-cbc-kan-mapping-homotopy-invariance] to the identity of each source to see that the enriched mapping complexes are Kan. Reverse the homotopy edges with outer horn fillers in these Kan complexes. The reversed homotopies give an equivalence edge in $\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$ directly: for vertices $(Y_x,H(x),Y_x)$ the enriched $(0,2)$ Hom of $\mathfrak C[\Delta^2]$ is $\Delta^1$, and the reversed homotopy from the identity to the composite supplies its map into $\operatorname{Fun}(Y_x,Y_x)$; the other homotopy supplies the triangle on $(H(x),Y_x,H(x))$. Thus $H$ lands in the full replete essential image $\mathcal T$ of $\iota$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-full-essential-image], in auxiliary universes containing these categories, to obtain a coherent quasi-inverse $L:\mathcal T\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$ and equivalences. Put $h^a=LH$ and write $v:\iota h^a\simeq H$ for the resulting equivalence. This constructs the small model rather than choosing its values independently. A quasi-inverse of $v_a$, applied to $\eta$, gives the distinguished point $\eta_0\in h^a(a)$ and a homotopy $v_a(\eta_0)\simeq\eta$. For every $Q:C\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U}$, the internal-hom definition in [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] gives the equality of full transformation spaces for two smaller-valued diagrams: every simplex of $C\times\Delta^n\to\mathcal S_{\mathcal U\prime}$ with these fixed-endpoint diagrams has all its vertices in the full smaller subcategory. Precomposition with $v$ and its inverse therefore identifies the larger evaluation equivalence of Step 3 with the required smaller one for $h^a,Q$, since evaluation at $\eta_0$ followed by $v_a$ is evaluation at $\eta$ up to the specified homotopy. To verify this on full mapping spaces, let $w$ be an inverse of $v$ in the functor quasicategory. The two composite precomposition maps are homotopic to precomposition by $vw$ and $wv$ by associativity in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], and then to identity maps by the inverse triangles and its unit laws. Thus actual composition with $v$ and $w$ gives the inverse maps and both homotopies. For any other small model with a specified equivalence to $H$, the same composition gives the same conclusion; uniqueness of a choice is not assumed. Applying that equivalence to the displayed homotopy of Step 4 yields precisely $f\mapsto Q(f)(q)$, with its full parameters, for the small-model covariant clause.

source.place: Theorem 4.8.4.1 on the full essential image; the universe inclusion is checked directly on enriched simplices. Agent-written size descent following the concrete comparison, preserving the original small value universe.

proof.text:
For the contravariant clause apply Steps 1--5 to $C=\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$, $Q=P$, and the object $a$. Opposite mapping-space conventions agree as spaces as follows. Put $U_D(x,y)=\{x\}\times_D\operatorname{Fun}(\Delta^1,D)\times_D\{y\}$. Reversal of the interval gives $U_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,x)=U_{\mathcal E}(x,a)^{\mathrm{op}}$. By [lem-coef-infinity-pinch-comparison] both right-pinched models map into these arrow spaces by natural homotopy equivalences. For a Kan complex $T$, reversal of barycentric coordinates gives a natural homeomorphism $|T^{\mathrm{op}}|\cong|T|$: it sends $[t,(r_0,\ldots,r_n)]$ to $[t,(r_n,\ldots,r_0)]$. The realization identifications of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones] make this well-defined, and it is its own inverse. It follows that $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}}(a,x)$ models $\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal E}(x,a)$ as a space. The coherent representable is the one on the opposite category, before taking this pointwise comparison; reversing the composition diagrams turns its postcomposition action into precomposition. In particular its distinguished point is still $\operatorname{id}_a$. Therefore the small-model evaluation equivalence of Step 5 becomes
$$\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}},\mathcal S)}(h_a,P)\simeq P(a).$$
The coherent small model on the opposite category is defined by Step 5, with its identity point corresponding to the singular identity. The arrow $a\to x$ in $\mathcal E^{\mathrm{op}}$ is $f:x\to a$ in $\mathcal E$, so the Step 4 inverse reads $p\mapsto(f\mapsto P(f)(p))$, with the same two inverse homotopies and simplicial parameter coherence. Only equivalences of models are used, not a strict identification of left- and right-pinched simplicial sets.

source.place: Remark 8.3.3.6, opposite duality; explicit interval and barycentric reversal checks retained.
